title: ST-depression–angina coupling does not reliably improve cross-center coronary disease prediction
abstract: A fixed ST-depression × exercise-angina interaction was tested beyond additive clinical/exercise measures in public angiography cohorts. Cleveland-trained models (303 participants) were evaluated without target fitting in VA Long Beach (200 participants). The interaction improved discovery out-of-fold log loss by 0.00442 but worsened external log loss by 0.01636 (paired fixed-model improvement interval −0.03072 to −0.00087). Joint training/test bootstrap improvement interval was −0.07152 to 0.00521. Spline, penalty, complete-case, zero-value and deduplication checks did not establish benefit. This negative result applies to one representation and historical selected cohorts; it does not prove absence of physiological symptom–electrical coupling or universal harm.
